channel.title: TCM Way
channel.description: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern mind — Bringing authentic Chinese medicine philosophy to the English-speaking world

item.title: Why the Ancients Said "Don't Hate the Sun" — and What We Lost When We Started Hiding From It
item.description: The Huangdi Neijing's Summer Chapter says "do not tire of the sun." Two thousand years later, modern science is proving the ancients right about sunlight, circadian rhythm, and why hiding from summer hurts us.

item.title: What a 2,000-Year-Old Springtime Guide Can Teach You About Reinvention
item.description: The Huangdi Neijing's Spring Chapter mapped renewal 2000 years ago — and its advice about going to bed late, rising early, and letting your hair down is startlingly relevant to our burnout culture.

item.title: What TCM Can Learn From Sourdough
item.description: A sourdough starter and your digestive system share a surprising secret. What TCM's Spleen theory reveals about microbial fermentation — and why your kitchen is the best pharmacy.

item.title: The One Ingredient In Your Kitchen That TCM Doctors Love
item.description: That knobby ginger root in your vegetable drawer is one of the most important herbs in TCM. Here's why — and exactly how to use it.

item.title: Move Like Water: Why Your Workout Might Be Working Against You
item.description: Your TCM body constitution determines what exercise heals you versus what drains you. Yang-deficient people need gentle warmth. Yin-deficient people need cooling movement. Damp-phlegm types actually thrive on HIIT.

item.title: Surviving the Hottest Days on Earth: What Ancient China Knew About Major Heat (大暑)
item.description: Before air conditioning, Chinese people used food as medicine to survive Major Heat — winter melon soup, coix seed water, and a counterintuitive truth: ice water makes you hotter.

item.title: The Season Your Body Is Actually In (It's Not The One On Your Calendar)
item.description: Your body doesn't run on the Gregorian calendar — it lives by five seasons. Summer is Fire season, and that July irritability? It's your Heart talking.

item.title: Eat With The Sun: The TCM Clock For Food
item.description: TCM's Meridian Clock says each organ has a 2-hour peak window — and eating in sync with it could be the simplest energy hack you've never tried.

item.title: How Ancient China Survived Summer Without Air Conditioning (And What That Teaches Us Today)
item.description: On Xiaoshu (Minor Heat), explore how ancient China survived brutal summers without AC — using mung bean soup, strategic napping, and a 2,000-year-old calendar tuned to the human body.

item.title: Your Anxiety Is Not in Your Head — Understanding the Liver Qi Connection
item.description: Your racing heart, the 3 AM wake-ups, the tightness in your chest — those are not just "in your head." Chinese medicine has been mapping the liver-emotion connection for 2,000 years.

item.title: How a Cold Becomes Cancer (Over Years)
item.description: A cold suppressed at the surface becomes a cancer decades later. The Shanghan Lun's six-stage map shows exactly how — and how to stop it. The final chapter in the Six Stages series.

item.title: When the Body Reaches Its Last Line — Understanding the Jueyin Stage
item.description: Hot flashes and ice-cold feet? Wired but exhausted? The Jueyin stage explains why your body feels like civil war — and what an 1,800-year-old formula can do about it.

item.title: The Fire Inside You Is Going Out (And You Don't Even Know It)
item.description: Always cold, bone-tired, and told everything is normal? Your body has a pilot light called the Life Gate Fire — and modern life is slowly blowing it out.

item.title: Stop Fighting — Start Warming: Why TCM's "Yang Tonics" Are Not About Heat
item.description: Modern medicine fights symptoms. TCM warms the furnace. Understanding how warming herbs restart your body's inner fire.

item.title: The Most Dangerous Quiet — Why "I Just Want to Sleep" Is Not Laziness
item.description: You want to sleep all the time, yet sleep doesn't restore you. Understanding the Shaoyin Stage — when disease reaches your body's deepest level and your vital fire is barely flickering.

item.title: When Food Stops Being Food — Understanding the Taiyin Stage
item.description: Food just sits there, bloating, exhaustion after eating — understanding the Taiyin Stage where your digestive engine fails and how to rekindle the fire.

item.title: When the Fire Won't Go Out — Understanding the Yangming Stage
item.description: High fever that won't quit, drenching sweats, and unquenchable thirst — understanding the Yangming Stage and Bai Hu Tang's powerful fire-extinguishing formula.

item.title: When Your Body Is Stuck Between Two Fires
item.description: Hot. Cold. Hot again. Your mouth tastes metallic. Welcome to the Shao Yang stage — where your body is caught between two fires, and Xiao Chai Hu Tang knows the way out.

item.title: Your Fever Might Be Your Friend
item.description: What if that high fever isn't a sign of failure, but a sign your body is fighting at full capacity? The Yangming stage and Bai Hu Tang reveal a counterintuitive truth.

item.title: Wind-Cold Is Not A Weather Report
item.description: Wind-Cold isn't about the weather. It's about how your body locks down when a pathogen invades the Taiyang layer — and why the sweat question changes everything about treating a cold.

item.title: Your Body Doesn't Need a Warrior — Stop Fighting, Start Warming
item.description: Stop declaring war on every cold. TCM's warming herbs — Gui Zhi, Gan Jiang, Fu Zi — build your inner fire so illness simply can't take hold. Ollie the Screech Owl explains why fluffing your feathers beats swinging a sword.

item.title: What Zhang Zhongjing Knew That Your Doctor Doesn't
item.description: In 200 AD, Zhang Zhongjing mapped six defensive layers — Taiyang, Shaoyang, Yangming, Taiyin, Shaoyin, Jueyin — that predict how illness moves through your body. Your doctor reads the transcript. He watched the live show. Both lenses matter.

item.title: Jing, Qi, Shen — The Three Treasures That Make You You
item.description: Your body has three layers: Jing (hardware), Qi (software), and Shen (user). Jing is the trust fund you were born with — finite, precious, and worth protecting. The Huangdi Neijing's conservation message is still urgently relevant today.

item.title: Your Body Is a Kingdom — Why Your Organs Aren't Just Parts
item.description: Your liver isn't just a filter. Your heart isn't just a pump. In the Huangdi Neijing, your body is a kingdom with five zang organs as department heads — and when one department goes rogue, the whole kingdom feels it.

item.title: The Five Elements Are Not a Personality Test — They're Your Body's Ecosystem
item.description: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water are not identity badges. They're functional relationships — a 2,000-year-old systems theory of how your organ systems feed and regulate each other. Your body is a garden ecosystem, not a filing cabinet.

item.title: Yin & Yang ≠ Good vs Evil — Why Balance Is the Point, Not the Battle
item.description: Yin and Yang aren't opponents on a scoreboard. The Huangdi Neijing describes them as a dynamic equilibrium — a seesaw that only works when both sides are free to move. Three classical principles explained for modern readers who've been sold the wrong metaphor.

item.title: Your Tongue Knows Before Your Blood Test Does
item.description: Your tongue is the only internal organ you can see without a scalpel. For 2,000 years Chinese medicine has read its color, shape, coating, and moisture like a dashboard — spotting patterns days or weeks before blood markers shift.

item.title: 10 Questions Ancient Chinese Doctors Asked (That Yours Never Will)
item.description: When was the last time a doctor asked whether your hands are warm or cold — and listened to the answer? Chinese medicine's Ten Questions diagnostic framework catches dysfunction years before any lab test. Here's what to ask yourself.

item.title: The Chinese Character for 'Medicine' Contains Music — What Ancient China Knew About Sound Healing
item.description: The Chinese character 藥 breaks down into 艹 (herbs) and 樂 (music). This isn't a coincidence. Ancient Chinese doctors had a five-tone healing system that mapped musical notes to internal organs — and modern neuroscience is catching up.

item.title: Your Shoulder Pain, Your IBS, Your Insomnia — They Might All Be Saying the Same Thing
item.description: You've seen the orthopedist for your shoulder. The gastroenterologist for your IBS. The psychiatrist for your anxiety. What if all five specialists were treating the same problem without knowing it?

item.title: It's Just a Cold — Why Chinese Medicine Thinks That's the Most Dangerous Sentence
item.description: Everyone says 'it's just a cold' and pops a pill. Chinese medicine sees a pathogen marching through your body's defenses — and if you ignore it, it doesn't forget where you live.

item.title: Stop Feeding What You're Trying to Fight — Why Chinese Medicine Is Skeptical of Supplements
item.description: You spend $50 a month on vitamins. Chinese medicine asks: who else are you feeding? The ancient insight that nutrition doesn't discriminate between you and your disease — and what to do instead.

item.title: The Castle Inside You: Your Body's 6-Layer Defense System
item.description: Your body doesn't just 'get sick.' It fights through six layers of defense, like an ancient castle. Understanding this map changes how you see every cold, every fever, every chronic illness.

item.title: Why Your Cold Hands Are Warning You
item.description: Cold hands aren't just 'poor circulation.' In TCM, they're an early warning system — and the most important cancer prevention sign you already have.

item.title: 6 Signs You're Actually Healthy (And Why Your Lab Results Don't Tell the Whole Story)
item.description: Your bloodwork came back 'normal.' So why do you still feel off? TCM has six health standards that catch problems years before any lab test would. Are you actually healthy?

item.title: That Heavy Feeling in Your Limbs? It's Not Laziness
item.description: Your arms feel like lead. You've been called lazy your whole life. TCM says it's not willpower — it's your Spleen asking for help, not judgment.

item.title: Your Body Runs on a Clock You Didn't Set — Why 3 AM Is Never Random
item.description: You wake up at 3 AM every night. Your appetite disappears at noon. You feel brain-foggy at 2 PM. Coincidence? TCM says your organs punch in and out on a schedule that's been running since before clocks existed.

item.title: Why Your Body Is Like a Traffic Jam (And How to Unstick Yourself)
item.description: That tight feeling in your chest, the sigh you can't suppress, the headache that won't quit — TCM calls it 'Qi stagnation.' Think of it as a traffic jam inside your body. Here's how to clear the lanes.

item.title: Qi Isn't Magic. It's Your Body's OS — Running Without Updates Since 200 BC
item.description: You've heard the word 'Qi' a thousand times. It's not mystical energy — it's your body's most practical operating system, explained 2,200 years ago in the Huangdi Neijing.

item.title: 8 Hours of Sleep, Still Wrecked? Your Organs Run a Night Shift — And Yours Called In Sick
item.description: You slept eight hours. You still feel wrecked. Traditional Chinese Medicine has a different answer — and it isn't 'sleep more.'

item.title: What a 1,800-Year-Old Book Taught Me About Anxiety — And Why the West Deserves to Hear It
item.description: In an age of accelerating AI and anxiety, the 1,800-year-old philosophy of the Shanghan Lun offers something our world desperately needs.
